name: To Kill a Mockingbird
hook: Harper Lee's only novel is Jeopardy's shorthand for Southern justice seen through a child's eyes.

facts.label: Harper Lee
facts.statement: Harper Lee, born in 1926 to an Alabama lawyer, published it in 1960 and won the Pulitzer Prize.

facts.label: Scout Finch
facts.statement: Scout, the narrator, is six-year-old Jean Louise Finch; her brother Jem is really Jeremy.

facts.label: Atticus Finch
facts.statement: Atticus Finch defends Tom Robinson, and his children are harassed by classmates for it.

facts.label: Boo Radley
facts.statement: Boo Radley is the reclusive neighbor Arthur Radley who saves Jem and Scout from Bob Ewell.

facts.label: Maycomb, Alabama
facts.statement: It is set in the fictional Alabama town of Maycomb, modeled on Lee's hometown of Monroeville.

facts.label: Truman Capote
facts.statement: Truman Capote, Lee's childhood friend, was the model for Dill.

facts.label: the 1962 film
facts.statement: The 1962 film starred Gregory Peck as Atticus and had John Williams as a studio pianist.
